body.text: Niraupamyastava
body.translated_text: <s>Niraupamyastava</s> (Hymn to the Incomparable)

body.text: ... kaṃ bhūtabhautikasadṛśaṃ sarvarūpacitrāṅgaṃsamuditaṃ kāyaṃ pratilabhate // sa sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣanṃaṇḍalānugataḥ kāyo dharmasvabhāvagatiṃgatatvān manomaya ity ucyate /
body.translated_text: ...obtains a body resembling the elements and material forms, endowed with all variegated limbs, fully arisen. That body, which accords with the assemblies of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, is called 'mind-made' (<s>manomaya</s>) because it has gone to the state of the true nature of <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: yadā cittaṃ manaś cāpi vijñānaṃ na pravartate /
children.translated_text: When mind (<s>citta</s>), thought (<s>manas</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) cease to operate,

children.text: tadā manomayaṃ kāyaṃ labhate buddhabhūmiṃ ca //
children.translated_text: then one obtains the mind-made body and the stage of <s>Buddha</s>hood.

body.text: iti vacanāt / niraupamyo bhagavāṃs / tathā sa sarvaśaś cittamanovijñānavikalpasaṃjñāpagato 'navagṛhīta ākāśasamo 'bhyavakāśaprakṛtito 'vatīrṇaś cānutpattikadharmakṣāntiprāpta ity ucyate / tatra bhavanto jinaputrāḥ evaṃ kṣāntisamanvāgato bodhisattvaḥ sahapratilambhād acalāyā bodhisattvabhūmer ga
body.translated_text: Thus it is said. The Blessed One is incomparable (<s>niraupamya</s>). Likewise, He has completely transcended the conceptions of mind, thought, and consciousness; He is unapprehended, equal to space, descended from the nature of open expanse, and is said to have attained the <s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). Therein, O sons of the Conqueror, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> endowed with such patience, from the very moment of attaining the Immovable (<s>Acalā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, reaches the pro-

body.text: ṃ
body.translated_text: -found

body.text: bhīraṃ bodhisattvavihāram anuprāpto bhavati durājñānam asaṃbhinnaṃ sarvanimittāpagatam ityādivacanān niḥsvabhavārthavedī / sa evaṃ kṣāntipratilabdho bodhisattvo yatra yatropasaṃkrāmati kṣatriyabrāhmaṇavaiśyaśūdradevabrahmapariṣadaṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇītīrthikamāraparṣadaṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattva</s> abode, which is difficult to comprehend, undifferentiated, and free from all marks — as stated in such passages — [thus] he is one who understands the meaning of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). That <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having attained such patience, wherever he approaches — whether assemblies of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, <s>Śūdras</s>, gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, monks, nuns, non-Buddhist ascetics, or <s>Māra</s>

body.text: sarvatrātīto niḥśaṅkam upasaṃkrāmati viśārada eva pravyāharati / tat kasmād dhetoḥ / sa hy anutpattikadharmakṣāntilābhāt sarvadharmānutpādākāreṇa sarvathā sarvaṃ pratividdhavāst
body.translated_text: — he approaches all of them without hesitation, having transcended all, and speaks with confidence. Why is that? Because through the attainment of <s>anutpattikadharma-kṣānti</s>, he has thoroughly penetrated everything in every way through the aspect of non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: u
body.translated_text: [continued]

body.text: .. mād asya aparajñānakṛtaṃ kleśakṛtaṃ ca parṣacchāradyaṃ nāstīti vaiśāradyaprāptaḥ anabhilāpyānabhilāpyakalpāyuḥpramāṇādhiṣṭhānatayā sa āyurvaśitāṃ labhate / cetovaśitām aprameyāsaṃkhyasamādhinidhyaptijñānapraveśanatayā / pariṣkāravaśitāṃ sarvalokadhātvanekavyūhālaṃkārapratimaṇḍitādhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśanatayā / karmavaśitāṃ yathākālaṃ karmavipākādhiṣṭhānasaṃdarśanatayā / upapattivaśitāṃ sarvalokadhātūpapattisaṃdarśanatayā / adhimuktivaśitāṃ ca pratilabhate sarvalokadhātubuddhapratipūrṇasaṃdarśanatayā / praṇidhānavaśitāṃ ca pratilabhate yatheṣṭabuddhakṣetralokābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanatayā / ṛddhivaśitāṃ sarvabuddhakṣetravikurvaṇasaṃdarśanatayā / dharmavaśitām anantamadhyadharmamukhālokasaṃdarśanatayā / jñānavaśitāṃ ca pratilabhate tathāgatabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmalakṣaṇānuvyañjanābhisaṃbodhisaṃdarśanatayā / ity evaṃ daśavaśitāprāpto yas tvaṃ dṛṣṭivipannasya lokasyāsya hitodyata ity anena ca praśastapratipattir ameyatvam acittatā coktā / vakṣyamāneṣv api sarveṣu pratyekam arthatrayaṃ yojyam / ata evoktaṃ bhagavatā / gambhīradharmakṣāntipāraṃgatair vaiśāradyaprāptair / dharmapravicayavibhaktinirdeśakuśalair
body.translated_text: ...therefore he has no timidity before assemblies caused by inferior knowledge or by defilements — thus he has attained fearlessness (<s>vaiśāradya</s>). He obtains mastery over lifespan (<s>āyurvaśitā</s>) through the power of sustaining an inexpressible number of eons of life; mastery over mind (<s>cetovaśitā</s>) through entering immeasurable and countless concentrations (<s>samādhis</s>) and contemplative knowledge; mastery over requisites (<s>pariṣkāravaśitā</s>) through displaying the adornment of manifold arrays in all world-realms; mastery over action (<s>karmavaśitā</s>) through displaying the maturation of <s>karma</s> at the appropriate time; mastery over birth (<s>upapattivaśitā</s>) through displaying birth in all world-realms; mastery over aspiration (<s>adhimuktivaśitā</s>) through displaying all world-realms filled with <s>Buddhas</s>; mastery over vows (<s>praṇidhānavaśitā</s>) through displaying awakening in desired <s>Buddha</s>-fields and worlds; mastery over miraculous powers (<s>ṛddhivaśitā</s>) through displaying transformations in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields; mastery over <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmavaśitā</s>) through displaying the illumination of endless and boundless gateways of <s>Dharma</s>; and mastery over knowledge (<s>jñānavaśitā</s>) through displaying the awakening to the marks and secondary marks of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s powers (<s>balas</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradyas</s>), and unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities. Thus, having attained the ten masteries (<s>daśavaśitā</s>), 'You who are devoted to the welfare of this world fallen into wrong views' — by this, his praiseworthy practice, immeasurability, and non-conceptuality are stated. In each of the verses to follow as well, the threefold meaning should be applied. Therefore the Blessed One has said: 'By those who have reached the far shore of patience regarding the profound <s>Dharma</s>, who have attained fearlessness, who are skilled in the analysis, classification, and exposition of <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: ity uktam / tatra dharmāś caturvidhā vipaśyanādharmāḥ skandhadhātvāyatanādayaḥ bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ smṛtyupasthānādayaḥ buddhadharmā daśabalavaiśāradyādayaḥ adhigamadharmāḥ śrotaāpattimārgaphalādayo yathākramam / etadbhedena catvāraḥ ślokā uktāḥ / tatra bauddhaṃ cakṣur dhyānābhisaṃskāranirvṛttam abhijñāsaṃgṛhītam aṣṭāvidhaparikarmalabhyatvāt kumārabhuvaḥ /
body.translated_text: ' — thus it is said. Therein, <s>dharmas</s> are of four kinds: <s>dharmas</s> of insight (<s>vipaśyanā</s>), namely the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), and so forth; <s>dharmas</s> conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>), namely the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>) and so forth; <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, namely the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), and so forth; and <s>dharmas</s> of attainment (<s>adhigama</s>), namely the path and fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpatti</s>) and so forth, respectively. In accordance with these divisions, four verses are stated. Therein, the <s>Buddha</s>-eye (<s>bauddha cakṣus</s>) is produced through the conditioning of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), included in the superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>), and because it is obtained through eightfold preparation, it belongs to the Prince [stage] (<s>kumārabhūmi</s>).

body.text: jñeyaṃ ca parikarmaiṣāṃ svabhāvānupalambhata
body.translated_text: And the preparation for these should be known through the non-apprehension of own-nature (<s>svabhāvānupalambha</s>)

body.text: iti / tenāpi cakṣuṣā tvayā na kiṃcid dṛṣṭaṃ saṃbhāvyate prāg evetaraiḥ / pañcānām api cakṣuṣām anavabhāsagamanatvāt tattvārthasya dṛṣṭijñānam / adarśanam eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ tattvārthadarśanam / nanu pratilabdhaprathamādibhuvo 'pi āryā na kaṃcid dharmam upalabhante tat ko 'syātiśaya ity āha / anuttarā ceti / yasmān nātra tattvārthadarśanād vyutthito bhavati / pūrvakās tu sapta vihārā vyāmiśrā ayam ekāntaśuddhaḥ / yathoktaṃ / yadā punaḥ sarvaprāyogikacaryāṃ vihāya saptamyā bhūmer aṣṭamīṃ bhūmim avakrānto bhavati tadā pariśuddhaṃ bodhisattvayānam abhirūhya ityādi / tasmād eva gambhīrāṇāṃ bodhisattvavihārāṇāṃ nānyo 'smād adhiko gaṃbhīro ity atrānuttarety ucyate // pravicayo lakṣaṇataḥ kṛtyato hetutaḥ phalataḥ saṃkhyāta āsvādata ādīnavato niḥsaraṇataś ca kleśato vyavadānataḥ parijñātaḥ prahāṇataḥ sākṣātkaraṇato bhāvanātaś ca / tatra yathākramaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus — even by that eye, nothing is seen as being possible [to apprehend], much less by the other [eyes]. Because the five eyes cannot illuminate [it], the knowledge-vision (<s>dṛṣṭijñāna</s>) of ultimate reality is precisely the non-seeing of all <s>dharmas</s> — that is the vision of ultimate reality. Now, if even the Noble Ones who have attained the first and subsequent stages do not apprehend any <s>dharma</s>, then what is the distinction here? To this he says: 'Unsurpassed' — because here one does not rise from the vision of ultimate reality. The previous seven abodes (<s>vihāras</s>) are mixed, [but] this one is exclusively pure. As it is stated: 'When, moreover, having abandoned all preparatory practice, from the seventh stage one descends to the eighth stage, then, having ascended the purified <s>bodhisattva</s>-vehicle...' and so forth. Therefore, among the profound <s>bodhisattva</s> abodes, there is none more profound than this — hence it is called 'unsurpassed' (<s>anuttara</s>). // The analytical investigation (<s>pravicaya</s>) [is] by way of characteristics, function, cause, result, enumeration, enjoyment, danger, escape, defilement, purification, full knowledge, abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation. Therein, in sequence

body.text: ṣaḍ / arthaviśeṣeṇa / arthadvayasaṃgrahenaikaḥ tathaivānyaḥ ekenaiko dvābhyām aparaḥ
body.translated_text: six [verses are allotted]. By distinction of meaning, one [verse] through the grouping of two meanings, likewise another; one by a single [meaning], another by two [meanings].

body.text: vikurvasi mahāṛddhyā māyopamasamādhinā
body.translated_text: You transform through great miraculous power, through the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s> (concentration)

body.text: ityādivacanāt / bhāvanārthena punar ekaḥ / tatrārūpavad ity ākāśavat / tathā coktaṃ yāvat tathāgatavaineyikānāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgatakāyavarṇarūpam ādarśayati / iti hi bho jinaputra yāvanto 'nabhilāpyeṣu buddhakṣetraprasareṣu sattvānām upapattyāyatanādhimuktiprasarās teṣu teṣu tathāgataḥ svakāyavibhaktim ādarśayati / sa sarvakāyavikalpasaṃjñāpagata ākāśamatāprāptaḥ / tac cāsya kāyasaṃdarśanam akṣūṇam avandhyaṃ ca sarvasattvaparipākavinayāyetyādi / vibhaktitaś catvāraḥ kāyatrayavibhāge ślokatrayaṃ / tathā hi saptamyāṃ bhūmau buddhakāyavyūhaṃ jānāti na tu tadā niṣpādayituṃ śaknoti / buddhakāyavyūhajñānāt tu tasyāṃ bhūmau niṣpādanecchāṃ jānāti / asyāḥ prabhṛti niṣpādayatīty āryadaśabhūmakādāv avagantavyam / karmāvaraṇapratipraśrabdhir ity uktam / etasyā eva kṣānteḥ sahapratilambhād yāny asya sugatidurgativipākyāni karmāvaraṇāni tāny asya samucchinnāni bhavanti / anyatra
body.translated_text: — thus and so forth it is stated. And one [verse] is in the sense of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). Therein, 'like the formless' means 'like space.' And thus it is said: '[He] displays to beings who are to be guided by the <s>Tathāgata</s> the color-form of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body.' For indeed, O son of the Conqueror, in as many inexpressible expanses of <s>Buddha</s>-fields as there are dispositions and inclinations of beings' places of rebirth, in each of those the <s>Tathāgata</s> displays the division of his own body. He has gone beyond all conceptions of bodily differentiation, having attained the nature of space. And that display of his body is undiminished and fruitful for the maturation and discipline of all beings — and so forth. By division, four [verses]: three verses on the threefold division of bodies (<s>kāyatrayavibhāga</s>). For on the seventh stage [the <s>bodhisattva</s>] knows the array of <s>Buddha</s>-bodies but cannot yet accomplish them at that point. However, through the knowledge of the array of <s>Buddha</s>-bodies on that stage, he knows the desire to accomplish [them]. From this [eighth stage] onward he accomplishes [them] — this should be understood from the Noble <s>Daśabhūmaka</s> and other [texts]. It is stated that the pacification of obstructions due to <s>karma</s> (<s>karmāvaraṇapratipraśrabdhi</s>) [occurs here] — because simultaneously with the attainment of this very patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), whatever obstructions due to <s>karma</s> ripening in good or bad destinies he had, those are completely cut off. Except

body.text: tathāgatānām anāgatajanatānukampadarśanād ata etadvibhāge ślokaḥ / karmaplutiḥ karmaṇo niṣyandaphalam / dharmadhātor acalitamānasattvād / vākkāyanirdeśatas trayaḥ // tatrotpādavigamān nityo nirodhavigamād dhruvaḥ śivo dvayābhāvāt / śivatvaṃ ca dvayākalpād iti vacanāt / kauśala ekaḥ / tatra manyanābhāvaḥ kliṣṭamanaḥparāvṛttyā / vikalpābhāvaḥ pravṛttivijñānaparāvṛttyā / iñjanābhāva ālayaparāvṛttyā / sarveṣv apy avasthitārthatrayopasaṃhāradvāreṇā bhagavato guṇānāṃ kīrtanena prasūtapuṇyasyāsyāṃ bhuvi sattvānāṃ pratiṣṭhāpanāya pariṇāmanārthenaika uktaḥ / tatra praśastagamanād punarāvṛttyā ca sugataḥ atarkyatvād alāpyatvād āryajñānād acintyatety acintyaḥ
body.translated_text: through the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' display of compassion for future beings — therefore one verse [is allotted] to the division of this [topic]. <s>Karmapluti</s> (karmic overflow) is the outflow-result (<s>niṣyandaphala</s>) of <s>karma</s>. Because his mind does not waver from the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality). Three [verses] by way of the exposition through speech and body. // Therein, 'eternal' (<s>nitya</s>) because of the absence of arising; 'permanent' (<s>dhruva</s>) because of the absence of cessation; 'blissful' (<s>śiva</s>) because of the absence of duality. And blissfulness is due to the absence of duality-construction, as the statement says. One [verse] on skill (<s>kauśala</s>). Therein, the absence of self-conceit (<s>manyanābhāva</s>) is through the transformation of the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭamanas</s>); the absence of conceptualization (<s>vikalpābhāva</s>) is through the transformation of the active consciousness (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>); the absence of agitation (<s>iñjanābhāva</s>) is through the transformation of the storehouse [consciousness] (<s>ālaya</s>). Through the recapitulation of the three established meanings in all [cases], one [verse] is stated for the purpose of dedicating the merit produced by the praise of the Blessed One's qualities, so as to establish beings on this stage. Therein, '<s>Sugata</s>' (Well-Gone) because of praiseworthy going and non-return; 'inconceivable' (<s>acintya</s>) because of being beyond reasoning and beyond expression, through noble knowledge.

body.text: aprameyaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Immeasurable' (<s>aprameya</s>)

body.text: aprameyāśrayaparāvṛttyā vibhutvalābhāt / tathā hy asyāṃ bhūmau nirantamahābodhisamudāgamaprayogasamādhiṣu vyavasthito bodhisattvo
body.translated_text: — because of the transformation of the immeasurable substratum (<s>āśraya</s>) and the attainment of sovereignty. For on this stage, the <s>bodhisattva</s> is established in <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions) of uninterrupted practice directed toward the great awakening.

body.text:
nityojjvalitabuddhiś ca kṛtyasaṃpādane 'gnivat /
śāntadhyānasamāpattisamāpannaś ca sarvadā /
body.translated_text: And [he is] one whose wisdom is ever blazing, like fire in accomplishing its task; and one who is always absorbed in the attainments of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) —

body.text: ity uktam // iti dvitīyasya samāsārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: thus it is said. // This concludes the summary meaning of the second [hymn]. //

body.text:
Acintyastava
idānīṃ tṛtīyāṃ vihārāvasthām adhikṛtyāha / svābhāvikī syād yadi vastusiddhir udīrṇadīpetaraśāntisiddhivat tadā sarvakleśamaheśvarasya carato mohasya śāntiḥ katham / ataḥ sarvathā sarvadṛṣṭīṇāṃ prahāṇāya
body.translated_text: <s>Acintyastava</s> (Hymn to the Inconceivable). Now, taking up the third stage of abiding (<s>vihāra</s>), he says: If the establishment of things were from their own nature — like the cessation of other [lights] being established when a blazing lamp [shines forth] — then how could there be cessation of delusion (<s>moha</s>), the great lord of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), which operates [everywhere]? Therefore, for the complete abandonment of all views in every way,

body.text: pratītyajānāṃ bhāvānāṃ naiḥsvābhāvyaṃ jagādaya ityādy āha / tatra navamyāṃ bodhisattva
body.translated_text: he declared the essencelessness (<s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s>) of things born through dependent origination — thus and so forth he says. Therein, on the ninth <s>bodhisattva</s>

body.text: bhūmau
body.translated_text: stage (<s>bhūmi</s>),

body.text: pratisaṃvidvihāraḥ /
body.translated_text: [there is] the abiding in analytical knowledge (<s>pratisaṃvidvihāra</s>).

body.text: iha bodhisattvas tenāpi vihāreṇa ga
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>bodhisattva</s>, unsatisfied even with that pro-

body.text: ṃ
body.translated_text: [continued]

body.text: bhīreṇāsaṃtuṣṭa uttarijñānaviseṣatām anugacchan yaiś ca dharmajñānābhisaṃskāraiḥ pareṣāṃ dharmaḥ sarvākāro bodhisattvena deśayitavyo yac ca dharmākhyānakṛtyaṃ tat sarvaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / tatredaṃ dharmasamākhyānakṛtyam / gahanopavicāreṣu ye ca saṃkliśyante viśuddhyante yena ca saṃkliśyante viśuddhyante yac ca saṃkleṣavyavadānaṃ yā ca tasyānaikāntikatā yā ca tasyaikāntikānaikāntikatā tasya yathābhūtajñānam / evaṃ ca deśanākuśalasya deśanākṛtyakuśalasya ca yat sarvākāramahādharmabhāṇakatvam ityādi yathāsūtram eva vistarato veditavyam / asamajñānam iti daśamyāṃ tathāgatakṛtyenāvasthitatvād yathoktam āryadaśabhūmake / yāvad daśānāṃ samādhyasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇāṃ paryante sarvajñajñānaviśeṣābhiṣekavān nāma bodhisattvasamādhir āmukhībhavatītyādi / yad adhikṛtyoktam /
body.translated_text: -found abiding, pursuing the distinction of higher knowledge — whatever <s>dharma</s>-knowledge and mental formations by which the <s>bodhisattva</s> should teach the <s>dharma</s> in all its aspects to others, and whatever the task of <s>dharma</s>-exposition — all of that he knows as it truly is. Therein, this is the task of <s>dharma</s>-exposition: those who become defiled and purified in impenetrable [conditions], by what means they become defiled and purified, what defilement and purification are, the non-exclusivity of that [process], and the exclusivity and non-exclusivity of that — his knowledge of all this as it truly is. Thus, his being a great expounder of <s>dharma</s> in all aspects, as one skilled in teaching and skilled in the task of teaching — this and so forth should be understood in detail as [stated] in the <s>sūtra</s> itself. 'Incomparable knowledge' — on the tenth [stage], because one is established in the activity of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, as stated in the Noble <s>Daśabhūmaka</s>: 'At the end of innumerable hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions) of the ten [stages], the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called "endowed with the consecration into the special knowledge of the omniscient" becomes manifest' — and so forth. With reference to which it is said:

children.translated_text: Due to the force of former penetration and the cessation of all conceptualization, he

children.text: na punaḥ kurute yatnaṃ paripākāya dehinām // 1
children.translated_text: no longer makes effort for the maturation of embodied beings. // 1

children.text: yo yathā yena vaineyo manyate 'sau tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Whoever is to be trained, however and by whatever means — that one is considered [to be trained] exactly so,
through teaching and the <s>rūpakāya</s> (form-body), through conduct, and through deportment. // 2
Effortlessly, with unobstructed understanding, always thus for him,
the welfare of beings proceeds in the world extending to the ends of space. // 3
A <s>bodhisattva</s> who has attained this state
approaches equality with <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the worlds regarding the liberation of beings. // 4

children.text: athā cāṇoḥ pṛthivyāś ca goṣpadasyodādheś ca yat /
children.translated_text: But the difference between an atom and the earth, or between a cow's hoof-print and the ocean —

children.text: antaraṃ bodhisattvānāṃ buddhasya ca tad antaram // 5
children.translated_text: that is the difference between <s>bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>Buddha</s>. // 5

body.text: iti
body.translated_text: Thus,

body.text: acintyam iti yathoktaṃ sa khalu bho jinaputra bodhisattva evam imāṃ bhūmim anugato 'cintyaṃ ca nāma bodhisattvavimokṣaṃ pratilabhate 'nāvaraṇaṃ cetyādi / vāggocarātītatareṣu vācām agocarair eva ca / piṇḍiteṣu rajāṃsi yāvanti guṇā daśamyāṃ bhavanti tāvanta ihāsya tāvad ity anidarśanam uktaṃ bhagavatyāṃ niṣṭhāgamanabhūmivyavasthitabodhisattvaguṇanirdeśe / māyāmarīcigandharvadakacandrasvapnapratibhāsapratiśrutkāpratibimbanirmāṇopamadharmādhimukter iti dṛṣṭāntāṣṭakenāṣṭāni lakṣaṇāni sūcitāni / tad yathā śūnyatālakṣaṇam animittalakṣaṇam apraṇihitalakṣaṇaṃ niḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ pratītyasamutpādalakṣaṇaṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇaṃ paratantralakṣaṇaṃ ca / tatra ṣadbhiḥ ṣadbhis tribhir deśanākṛtyārthabhedena yathākramaṃ trīṇi lakṣaṇāny uktāni / ekenaiṣām eva trayāṇām upasaṃhāraḥ ṣadbhiḥ saptabhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saptabhiś ca śeṣāniboddhavyāni / iti māyādidṛṣṭāntair ityādi saptabhiḥ ślokair yathākramaṃ guṇakathanamukhena sarveṣām upasaṃhāraḥ kām apy acintyāṃ paramagambhirāvasthāṃ prāptatvād asya vihārasyeti bhavaddṛśā eva bhavantaṃ janayantīti pratipādanāyaikaḥ // asyām eva bhuvi sattvānāṃ pratiṣṭhāpanāya puṇyapariṇāmanam ity anyaḥ // //
body.translated_text: 'inconceivable' (<s>acintya</s>) — as stated: 'That <s>bodhisattva</s> indeed, O son of the Conqueror, having entered this stage thus, obtains the <s>bodhisattva</s>-liberation named "inconceivable" and "unobstructed"' — and so forth. 'Having transcended the range of speech' — indeed by what is itself beyond the range of speech. 'Having been condensed' — as many dust-particles [as there are], so many qualities exist on the tenth [stage]; 'so many here for him, so much' — thus the impossibility of demonstration is stated in the <s>Bhagavatī</s>, in the exposition of qualities of a <s>bodhisattva</s> established on the stage of final attainment. 'With the conviction that <s>dharmas</s> are like illusion, a mirage, a <s>gandharva</s>-city, water-moon, a dream, an apparition, an echo, a reflected image, and a magical creation' — through these eight similes, eight characteristics are indicated, namely: the characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the characteristic of signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), the characteristic of wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), the characteristic of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>), the characteristic of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), and the characteristic of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). Therein, by [groups of] six, six, and three, according to the divisions of the purpose of the teaching-task, three characteristics are stated in sequence. By one [simile], these very three are recapitulated. By [groups of] six, seven, six, and seven, the remaining [characteristics] should be understood. Thus, 'by similes such as illusion and so forth' — through seven verses, in sequence, by way of praise of qualities, all are recapitulated. One [verse] is for demonstrating that 'beings like you themselves give birth to [one like] you' — because [the bodhisattva] has attained an inconceivable, supremely profound state in this abiding. And another [verse] is for the dedication of merit for establishing beings on this very stage.

body.text: tṛtīyasya samāsārthaḥ // //
body.translated_text: The summary meaning of the third [<s>stava</s>] (hymn).

body.text:
Paramārthastava
phalāvasthām ārabhya sarva evānāśravā dharmāḥ sarvaprakārām anuttarāṃ viśuddhim upagatavantaḥ saṃbuddhākhyāṃ pratilabhante / teṣāṃ hetvavasthāyām eva tāvad aśūnyatā prāg eva phalāvasthāyām ity āha // kathaṃ stoṣyāmi te nāthetyādi / anutpannam anālayam iti anutpannasvabhāvenetyāder yāvad gambhīrāya namo 'stu ta ity etadantasya sūcanam // vāk vācāṃ panthāś ca saṃkalpaḥ / tayor atīto gocaro yena / tathā coktam acintyam anidarśanam iti / tathāpītyādinā saṃvṛtyā parihāraḥ / abhimukhyāḥ prabhṛti viśeṣataḥ pratilabdhānām anutpādādīnāṃ niratiśayārthena pañca tasyāḥ prabhṛti nirodhalābhād āvaraṇadvayavāsanāśeṣasyāpy abhāvāt paramagāmbhīryārthenaikaḥ / evaṃ stute stuto bhūyāḥ saṃvṛtyeti śeṣaḥ athavā kiṃ bata stutaḥ paramārthena / kiṃśabda ākṣepe bataśabdo 'vadhāraṇeneva cety arthaḥ / tam eva pratipādayati stutyetyādi / idānīṃ saṃvṛtyāpi stuter asaṃbhavaṃ pratipādayann āha / kas tvāṃ śaknoti saṃstotum ityādi / utpādavyayavarjito bhagavān stotā cotpādavyayayuktaḥ / anādyantamadhyo bhagavān / sa ca trikāṇḍapratītyasamutpādasaṃgṛhītaḥ / grāhakagrāhyanirmukto bhagavān sa ca grāhake grāhye ca caratīti / saṃvṛtyāpi bhūtaguṇākhyānarūpāyāḥ stuter asaṃbhavaḥ / acintyapratītyasamutpādadharmatayā saty advaye 'pi prakṛter abhāvād iti // svabhāvapariśuddhyadhimuktyāpi vastuno
body.translated_text:
<s>Paramārthastava</s> (Hymn to Ultimate Reality)
Beginning from the stage of fruition, all undefiled (<s>anāśrava</s>) <s>dharmas</s> have attained complete purity (<s>viśuddhi</s>) in every respect and obtain the designation '<s>saṃbuddha</s>' (Fully Awakened One). Their non-emptiness (<s>aśūnyatā</s>) exists already at the causal stage — how much more so at the stage of fruition. Thus he says: 'How shall I praise you, O Lord...' and so forth. '[You who are] unborn, without substratum (<s>anālaya</s>)' — this indicates [the passage] from 'having an unborn own-nature' up to 'Homage to you, the profound one.' Speech (<s>vāk</s>) and the path of speech (<s>vācāṃ panthāḥ</s>) refer to conception (<s>saṃkalpa</s>). [The Blessed One is He] whose domain transcends both of these. As it is also said: 'Inconceivable, without indication.' [The verse beginning] 'Nevertheless...' and so forth provides an answer from the standpoint of conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). From the sixth stage (<s>Abhimukhī</s>) onward, non-arising and the other [qualities] that are specifically attained — five [verses are allotted] to [those stages] in the sense of unsurpassed meaning, because from the fifth [stage] onward the cessation-attainment is gained and even the residual traces of the two obstructions (<s>āvaraṇadvayavāsanā</s>) are absent; one [verse is allotted] in the sense of supreme profundity. 'When praised thus, may you be praised' — the remainder is: 'conventionally.' Or alternatively: 'Why indeed (<s>kiṃ bata</s>) has [He] been praised?' — in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārtha</s>). The word <s>kiṃ</s> expresses censure, and the word <s>bata</s> [expresses] emphasis, as it were — such is the meaning. This very [point] he demonstrates with 'Through praise...' and so forth. Now, demonstrating the impossibility of praise even conventionally, he says: 'Who can praise you?' and so forth. The Blessed One is devoid of arising and cessation, while the praiser is subject to arising and cessation. The Blessed One is without beginning, end, or middle; and the [praiser] is encompassed within the three temporal phases (<s>trikāṇḍa</s>) of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination). The Blessed One is free from the apprehender and the apprehended (<s>grāhakagrāhya</s>), while [the praiser] operates within apprehender and apprehended — therefore, even conventionally, praise in the form of narrating true qualities is impossible, because in the absence of own-nature even in [seeming] non-duality, due to the character of inconceivable <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>.

body.text: 'nupalambliena pravṛttas tu mahāphala iti / mahān asaṃbhavo bhavatīti pratyetavyam // sugatapadaprāpaṇāya puṇyapariṇāmanārthenaikaḥ // etāvantam evārtham adhikṛtyābhisamayakramaḥ prajñāpāramitādiṣu vistareṇokto boddhavyaḥ // // iti caturthasya samāsārthaḥ //
body.translated_text: One who proceeds through the non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) even of conviction in the purity of own-nature of things obtains great fruit — thus it should be understood that [this] great impossibility [of praise] obtains. One [verse is allotted] for the purpose of dedicating merit (<s>puṇyapariṇāmanā</s>) so as to lead [beings] to the state of the <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One). This concludes the summary meaning of the fourth [hymn]. The sequence of realization (<s>abhisamayakrama</s>) pertaining to this entire subject-matter should be understood as extensively taught in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and other [texts].

body.text: catuḥstavasamāsārthaḥ paṇḍitāmṛtākarasyeti // //
body.translated_text: [End of] the <s>Catuḥstavasamāsārtha</s> (Summary Meaning of the Four Hymns) by the scholar <s>Amṛtākara</s>.
